verdict: The script contains remote code execution via eval and uncontrolled script loading, making it unsafe for payment pages
summary: The widget dynamically loads scripts from a URL parameter, evaluates arbitrary code from postMessage, and exfiltrates PII via beacon and insecure pixel. These behaviors violate PCI DSS 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 and raise privacy concerns.

text: Loads external script from URL parameter (sb_lang) and appends to document head
Listens for postMessage events and executes received code via eval
Collects email, phone, cookies, URL, referrer, UA, language, timezone and sends to api.supportbubble.io via navigator.sendBeacon
Sends an insecure HTTP image pixel to px.supportbubble.io with a client identifier

data: email, phone, session cookie, page URL, referrer, user agent, language, timezone

title: Remote code execution via eval on untrusted postMessage
impact: Allows an attacker controlling the postMessage to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the page context, enabling credential theft or further compromise
recommendation: Remove eval usage; replace with a whitelist of allowed commands or a safe message protocol

title: Uncontrolled script injection via URL parameter
impact: An attacker can supply any URL, causing the browser to load and execute attacker‑controlled JavaScript, facilitating Magecart style skimming
recommendation: Validate the parameter against a whitelist of trusted domains or remove dynamic loading entirely

title: PII exfiltration without user consent
impact: Collects personally identifiable information and transmits it to a third‑party endpoint, violating GDPR/CCPA consent requirements
recommendation: Obtain explicit consent before collecting/shipping PII; limit data to only what is necessary

title: Insecure mixed‑content tracking pixel
impact: Loads HTTP resource on HTTPS page, exposing the request to network tampering and leaking client identifier
recommendation: Serve the pixel over HTTPS and consider CSP upgrade‑insecure‑requests

title: Wildcard postMessage broadcast
impact: Any ancestor frame can receive configuration data, potentially exposing internal state
recommendation: Restrict targetOrigin to a specific trusted origin

pci: Fails PCI DSS 6.4.3 (no secure coding for remote code execution) and 11.6.1 (no monitoring of malicious code); not safe for payment pages
privacy: Collects personal data and sends to third‑party without consent, violating GDPR/CCPA

text: Eliminate eval(e.data.code) and replace with a safe command handler
Stop loading external scripts from the sb_lang query parameter or enforce strict whitelist
Change wildcard postMessage targetOrigin to a specific trusted domain
Log and monitor all outbound beacon and pixel requests for anomalous activity
Serve the tracking pixel over HTTPS and add CSP upgrade‑insecure‑requests

policy: script-src 'self' https://cdn.supportbubble.io; connect-src 'self' https://api.supportbubble.io; img-src 'self' https://px.supportbubble.io;
notes: Only allow scripts from the known CDN and restrict connections to the API endpoint. Do not whitelist wildcard origins.
